Below are recommended actions and a template you can use to request formal authorization for a forensic investigation.

Recommended immediate actions (preserve evidence)
- Stop any log rotation or deletion processes and make secure copies (snapshots) of relevant systems to preserve evidence.
- Take forensic images of affected endpoints and servers rather than working on live systems where possible.
- Preserve email/mailbox data (including deleted items) and relevant mail server logs/headers.
- Preserve file system metadata and original complaint file(s) as submitted (including timestamps, document metadata).
- Preserve DLP/exfiltration alerts, VPN/proxy/firewall logs, SSO/authentication/audit logs, and endpoint detection logs.
- Preserve physical access logs/CCTV if the complaint could have been printed or handled physically.
- Maintain detailed chain-of-custody documentation for every copy and access to evidence.

Logs and data sources to collect (for authorized investigators)
- Mail server/ESMTP logs and original message headers (Received headers, originating IP).
- Document management system access logs (who created/modified/downloaded the file, IP, timestamps).
- File metadata (author, last-saved-by, embedded metadata) and file properties.
- DLP, CASB, or content-sharing logs (links shared externally, uploads to cloud storage).
- VPN/proxy/firewall logs for relevant timestamps and IP addresses.
- Authentication/SSO logs (successful/failed logins, token issuances).
- Endpoint logs and forensic images (file-open events, USB attachments, print spooler history).
- Print/scan device logs if physical copies were used.
- Mailbox rules/forwarding and access permissions for recipient mailboxes.
- CCTV/physical access logs if physical handling is possible.

Procedural/legal protections and steps
- Escalate immediately to HR, Legal/Compliance, and Information Security. Do not disclose any potential reporter identity to the accused without legal advice.
- Obtain written authorization that defines scope, purpose, authorized personnel, and retention and disclosure rules.
- If applicable, involve an external digital forensics firm to ensure impartiality and preserve admissibility.
- Follow applicable laws and internal policy about whistleblower confidentiality and retaliation.
- Prepare a report for HR/Legal with findings and recommended remedial actions; they will determine whether identity may be disclosed and to whom.

- Purpose: Authorize a forensic investigation to determine the source and pathway of a confidential complaint leak.
- Scope: Systems to be imaged/logs collected (list mail servers, file servers, endpoints, DLP logs, VPN, etc.), time window, and exclusions.
- Authorized personnel: Names/roles of internal investigators and any external vendor.
- Confidentiality: Investigation findings to be restricted to HR/Legal/Compliance and investigators; no disclosure to accused without legal approval.
- Chain of custody and evidence handling requirements.
- Approval (name/title/date/signature).

- Draft an email to HR/Legal/IT recommending the above steps.
